docs.text: Analysis amendment, round 5 (2026-10-01) ¶ Status: retrospective, after results and the round 4 independent review. The archived plan and its SHA-256 remain unchanged; chronology is not independently established. Incident clocks now honor explicit AM/PM: 12 AM is midnight and 12 PM is noon. Without a marker, valid clocks use 24-hour time. Consistent 13-23 PM and 0 AM inputs retain their 24-hour meaning. 0 PM is unresolved because its source convention is ambiguous; 13-23 AM conflicts. Missing/malformed clocks or unknown markers also remain null, with a per-row reason and an aggregate QA flag. The separate incident date is retained. This does not change calendar-year splits, co-reported rainfall pairing or plausibility eligibility; no time-zone/weather join is asserted. Normalized rows are regenerated privately, not distributed. Retain the threshold implementation: positive at or above the eligible 2022-2024 training rainfall 75th percentile, using at least three observations per identifier. Unsupported identifiers retain an infinite threshold and default negative; missing test rainfall is excluded. Export support and denominators. In this snapshot, 1,635 of 1,643 test report rows have threshold support; eight rows across five identifiers default negative. The fraction stays 395/1,643. Five rows equal their threshold. This describes reported events only, without non-event-day detection or accuracy claims. QA exports distinguish identifier missingness counts (>50% within an identifier) from report-row flags, report full-feed denominators and unique quarantine counts, and disclose overlapping flags. Neither missingness nor unresolved times changes eligibility for the current calendar-year analysis. All four headline values, intervals, denominators and rankings are unchanged. See the local verification receipt and regenerated cohort ledger for measured checks.

docs.text: Preregistration: CSO Insight evaluation ¶ Frozen: 2026-10-01 (before any pipeline results) Question ¶ How well does a rainfall-normalized per-outfall model rank CSO outfalls and predict overflow volume compared to simple baselines on hold-out years? Data ¶ Primary dataset: Massachusetts EEA combined sewer overflow notifications CSV ( https://openamend.org/data/EEADP_CSO.csv ). Events included: Rows where eventType contains "CSO". Rainfall: Co-reported rainfallData field (inches, converted to mm). No model-assisted relabelling. Volume: Co-reported volumnOfEvent field (US gallons, converted to m3). Splits (fixed before results) ¶ Split Years Purpose Train 2022, 2023 Fit rainfall-response models and ranking Validation 2024 Model selection (not used for final headline metrics) Test 2025 Headline hold-out metrics Rows from 2026 are excluded from evaluation splits (partial year). Methods ¶ Clean and normalize units (gallons to m3, inches to mm). Align events where both volume and rainfall are present. Fit log-linear rainfall response per outfall (minimum 5 paired observations). Rank outfalls by bootstrap resampling of events (500 samples, seed 42) for frequency and total volume. Flag data quality: >50% missing volume or rainfall per outfall, negative values, duration >72 h. Baselines (official simple rules) ¶ ID Rule Implementation B1 Event count ranking Count raw events per outfall on test year B2 Mean volume Predict constant mean volume per outfall from train+validation B3 Rainfall threshold Predict overflow when rainfall exceeds training 75th percentile for that outfall Metrics ¶ Metric Definition Unit spearman_trainval_vs_test_frequency Spearman correlation between train+validation frequency ranks and test-year counts dimensionless rmse_rainfall_model_m3 RMSE of rainfall-response volume predictions on test events with paired data m3 rmse_mean_volume_baseline_m3 RMSE of B2 on same test events m3 rain_threshold_positive_rate Fraction of B3 positive predictions on test events proportion All metrics reported with bootstrap 95% intervals (500 resamples, seed 42). Scoring integrity tests ¶ Perfect rank agreement must score Spearman rho = 1.0. Empty comparison must return no score. Stop rules ¶ If test-year events < 100, stop and report (do not claim generalization). If fewer than 10 outfalls have paired volume+rainfall in train+validation, stop. If bootstrap RMSE CIs are undefined (NaN), stop. Uncertainty ¶ Bootstrap resampling unit = individual CSO events (not outfalls alone), preserving per-outfall structure within each resample. What we will not do ¶ Tune splits after seeing test metrics. Label data with this package's parsers and call it manual ground truth. Compare model rerun to itself as inter-rater agreement. Expected outputs ¶ results/evaluation.json results/report.html RESULTS.md Figures under results/figures/ Hardware ¶ Apple M3 Ultra, local execution only.

docs.text: Preregistration amendment (2026-10-01) ¶ Status: Results had already been computed before this amendment was written. What changed ¶ RMSE estimand: Clarified that both the rainfall model and mean-volume baseline are scored on the same pooled test events with paired volume and rainfall. RMSE is pooled across events (not macro-averaged per outfall). Bootstrap resampling unit remains individual CSO events. Spearman estimand: Clarified that the point estimate is the direct observed Spearman correlation over the union of outfalls (absent outfalls score zero). Bootstrap resamples train+validation events to quantify ranking uncertainty. Plausibility quarantine: Events with rainfall above 254 mm (10 inches), volume above 37,854 m3 (10 million US gallons), or other implausible values are excluded from fitting and headline descriptive totals under documented rules added after data-quality review. Exclusion counts and sensitivity are exported to results/cohort_summary.json . Rain threshold metric: Missing test rainfall is excluded (unknown), not imputed as zero. Why ¶ Independent publication review found the original implementation averaged per-outfall RMSE on different cohorts, double-bootstrapped Spearman replicates, and did not enforce stop rules. Frozen preregistration ¶ The original docs/PREREGISTRATION.md and its SHA-256 remain unchanged. This amendment supplements it.

docs.text: Data manifest ¶ Inventory and rights assessment updated 2026-10-01. Public outputs are factual aggregate summaries of utility-reported Massachusetts CSO report rows, with source attribution. They are not independently verified physical discharges. Massachusetts feed ¶ Field Value Owner Massachusetts EEA / MassDEP, archived by the Archive of Massachusetts Environmental Data (AMEND) Acquisition AMEND CSV Source page EEA portal archive Snapshot SHA-256 0e8a56ebf1870646431de7c1d326065fbcd9cd27f63132e0790e79eb5ef231c3 Snapshot size 5,114,767 bytes; 16,720 CSO report rows after event-type filter Classes retained Public Notification Report and Verified Data Report; other classes retained if present Counting unit Report rows; stages may produce multiple reports for a discharge The AMEND dataset page describes a freely distributed public-source database (checked 2026-10-01). No separate dataset-specific licence was found in the reviewed page. A second check on 2026-10-11 found none either: the AMEND data page and its about page state no licence, and the project's source repository ( nesanders/MAenvironmentaldata ) declares none (GitHub repository licence field empty and no licence file, read 2026-10-11 00:35 PT). We therefore treat the AMEND files as unlicensed copies of Massachusetts public records: this repository ships no AMEND file, only the derived aggregates listed below, with attribution. The MassDEP policies provide a public-record reuse basis with copyright exceptions; direct access on 2026-10-01 returned 403, so no new blanket permission verification is asserted. The exact shipped fields are computed counts by class/year/identifier, summed volumes, aggregate flag-type counts, bootstrap intervals, support counts and evaluation statistics. Our basis for these outputs is factual aggregation of public records, not a grant to relicense the upstream database. No upstream prose, map tiles or analysis implementation is copied. Attribution is retained in every JSON/HTML/PNG output and in documentation; design licences apply to our original expression only. The clean public snapshot procedure in RELEASE.md omits that history without rewriting it. Licence boundary ¶ Code is Apache-2.0 (root LICENSE). Original documentation and figure design are CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0.txt). These declarations do not license upstream data, third-party works or database rights. Source facts are attributed to MassDEP via AMEND; rights remain with their owners. Do not infer an unconditional dataset grant. Other referenced datasets and research ¶ Resource Use and redistribution EPA ECHO Link/context only; no content shipped Metro Vancouver map Link/context only; no tiles, records or reports shipped NYC annual CSO report Link only; PDF withheld AMEND/SWMM/PySWMM research/software Citations only; no upstream implementation or paper text shipped Snapshot recovery ¶ The live AMEND route refreshes; a hash pin detects changes but cannot ensure perpetual availability. Preserve a lawful private copy of the exact snapshot with this digest. If live acquisition no longer matches, obtain that snapshot from the data owner or an independently permitted archive, place it at data/raw/ma_eea_cso.csv and run cso-insight run --root . --skip-download . The pipeline verifies the same hash before analysis. Never reseal a changed feed as this result. If no matching copy is available, this analysis cannot be regenerated; report that acquisition limitation. The release contains no raw snapshot and makes no immutable-download guarantee. Preservation during acquisition ¶ ./scripts/download_data.sh [destination] writes a temporary sibling, verifies the pinned hash, then atomically swaps into a separate acquisition path. Its default is data/raw/ma_eea_cso.download.csv . It refuses the frozen data/raw/ma_eea_cso.csv , including aliases and hard links. Network/hash failures preserve existing files. The Python pipeline also verifies a temporary download before replacement; the helper never overwrites the frozen snapshot. If the frozen path is absent, a permitted matching acquisition can be installed with test ! -e data/raw/ma_eea_cso.csv && cp -n data/raw/ma_eea_cso.download.csv data/raw/ma_eea_cso.csv . Then run cso-insight run --root . --skip-download , which verifies the hash again. A changed feed requires a separately versioned analysis. Never change this pin to make reproduction pass; recover a matching permitted snapshot or stop.

docs.text: Results ¶ Case study summary ¶ Massachusetts EEA CSO notifications (2022 to 2025 hold-out on 2025) show stable report-row counts across identifiers (Spearman 0.8510) but the simple mean-volume baseline beats the log1p rainfall model on pooled RMSE (4801.3 vs 12210.4 m3). Descriptive volume totals exclude notifications above a 10 million gallon plausibility cap; cohort_summary.json reports a 32.1% volume reduction from that filter. Headline metrics ¶ Hold-out test year 2025. Spearman n counts identifiers, including UNKNOWN permittee buckets. RMSE n counts model-scorable paired report rows; multiple reports may describe one discharge. Rainfall threshold is positive at or above the eligible training+validation 75th percentile (at least three rainfall observations per identifier). Of 1643 eligible known-rainfall test report rows, 1635 have threshold support; 8 rows across 5 identifiers default negative because support is insufficient. These rows remain in the denominator; missing rainfall is excluded. This event-conditional fraction does not measure overflow detection or accuracy on non-event days. Intervals are conditional event-bootstrap ranges, not storm-blocked inference. spearman_trainval_vs_test_frequency : 0.8510 (95% CI [0.8302, 0.8543], n=171) rmse_rainfall_model_m3 : 12210.4286 (95% CI [7100.5400, 16489.1477], n=1625) rmse_mean_volume_baseline_m3 : 4801.3013 (95% CI [4454.0005, 5197.9809], n=1625) rain_threshold_positive_rate : 0.2404 (95% CI [0.2200, 0.2608], n=1643) Cohort flow ¶ Stage Report rows CSO feed (all classes) 16720 Eligible across full feed 16544 Eligible 2022-2025 15122 Eligible 2025 3075 Eligible paired 2025 1643 Model-scorable paired 2025 (same rows for baseline) 1625 Reporting class (full feed) Rows Missing volume or rain Public Notification Report 8059 8058 Verified Data Report 8661 0 Reporting stages are retained separately; the estimand is report rows, not distinct discharges. Volume-cap exclusions: 156 evaluation-period reports; 159 across the full feed. The volume-cap sensitivity uses 2022-2025 volume after other eligibility filters, relative to the same cohort with the volume cap relaxed. The cohort ledger records unknown identifier buckets and model-support exclusions by identifier. Volume-cap sensitivity ¶ Observed volume rank With cap Without volume cap 1 NEW023 MWR203 2 FAL013 NEW023 3 HOL09 HOL09 4 FAL011 WOR001 5 SPR010 LOW008 Removing high-volume reports changes priorities; the uncapped leader can disappear from the capped top five. These filters flag suspect values and do not verify errors. Reproduce ¶ cso-insight run --root . Hardware: Darwin arm Baselines ¶ event_count_ranking: rank by raw event count per outfall (no rainfall model) (cso-insight-baseline/1.0) mean_volume_per_event: predict arithmetic mean volume per outfall from train+validation (cso-insight-baseline/1.0) rainfall_threshold: positive when rainfall is at or above training+validation 75th percentile; fewer than 3 training rainfall observations default negative (cso-insight-baseline/1.0) Descriptive totals and uncertainty ¶ MassDEP via AMEND, pinned snapshot; 2022-2025 eligible report rows. Points are observed totals; bars show conditional bootstrap intervals on metrics, not rank positions. Counts can include multiple reporting stages of one discharge. Volume caps can change priorities: inspect the capped/uncapped top-five comparison in the cohort ledger. Original figure design CC BY 4.0; upstream rights retained.

docs.text: Technical report: CSO Insight ¶ Abstract ¶ We present an open Python pipeline that ingests public combined sewer overflow (CSO) report-row data, aligns co-reported rainfall, flags implausible values, fits per-outfall log1p rainfall-response models, ranks outfalls descriptively with bootstrap uncertainty on counts and volumes, and evaluates amended hold-out baselines. The frozen analysis plan is amended retrospectively; pre-result registration is unverified, and results were seen before the 2026-10-01 amendment clarified estimands. Rainfall-normalized outfall ranking was not evaluated. 1. Problem ¶ Combined sewer systems discharge diluted wastewater during wet weather. Utilities must monitor overflows, report trends, and prioritize outfalls for intervention. Metro Vancouver publishes a real-time overflow map; this demonstration uses Massachusetts data and makes no claim about other local data routes. Analysts need reproducible methods that work on whatever open data exists. 2. Related work ¶ EPA SWMM ( epa.gov ): physics-based simulation requiring local network models. PySWMM ( JOSS 10.21105/joss.02292 ): Python interface to SWMM engines. McGrath et al. (2019) : network topology and rainfall controls on CSO variability, doi:10.1029/2019WR025336 . AMEND dashboard ( openamend.org/dashboard.html ): CSV-backed discharge analysis, external rainfall alignment and reporting-quality views on the Massachusetts feed. Regulatory reporting : EPA ECHO sewer overflow CSVs (partial US coverage). AMEND already has Python tests and automated chart regeneration; see its analysis script , tests and workflows at immutable commit b0a5c729abb41ba77b24ec0f6df835eee0a5887f (identified by the independent round 4 review; links pinned here). This package performs no external meteorological join. This package integrates notification ingestion, QA quarantine, descriptive ranking, cohort accounting and amended hold-out evaluation in one reproducible command. AMEND and this package overlap in report aggregation and plotting. This library complements AMEND's analysis with its packaged typed API, explicit cohort ledger and amended evaluation; hydraulic simulation remains a separate task. 3. Data ¶ Primary: Massachusetts EEA CSO notifications ( https://openamend.org/data/EEADP_CSO.csv ). See docs/DATA_MANIFEST.md . Statistic Value CSO rows 16,720 Distinct outfall IDs 171 (169 named plus two synthetic UNKNOWN buckets) Evaluation years 2022 to 2025 (2026 partial, excluded; 2022 begins July 2) Rows with volume and rainfall (eligible) see results/cohort_summary.json Rainfall is co-reported in inches ( rainfallData ); volume in US gallons ( volumnOfEvent ). These are utility-reported fields, not independently verified labels. Both notification and verified reporting stages are retained; matching stages are not reconciled into distinct discharges. All count results concern report rows. Missingness is structured by reporting stage: 8,058 of 8,059 notification-stage rows lack one or both measurements; no verified-stage rows do in this snapshot. The ledger exports period/class denominators, date ranges, and verified-only count sensitivity. UNKNOWN identifiers pool missing outfall IDs by permittee; they are not physical outfalls. Metro Vancouver: Real-time map only via the route reviewed; annual PDF tables. Documented as regional context; not used as primary data. 4. Methods ¶ Cleaning: Convert gallons to m3, inches to mm; parse treatment categories explicitly. Honor AM/PM (12 AM midnight, 12 PM noon); valid unmarked clocks use 24-hour time. Consistent 13-23 PM and 0 AM retain their 24-hour meaning. Ambiguous 0 PM, conflicting 13-23 AM, missing/malformed clocks and unknown markers remain null and are flagged; the separate date is retained. No time-zone or weather-time join is asserted. Quarantine: Exclude events with rainfall above 254 mm (10 inches), volume above 37,854 m3 (10 million US gallons), negative values, or duration above 72 h from fitting and headline descriptive totals. These are declared plausibility filters, not verified error labels. Exclusion counts and volume sensitivity are exported to results/cohort_summary.json . Alignment: Retain eligible events with both volume and rainfall for modelling. Rainfall response: Per outfall, fit log1p(volume) ~ rainfall via OLS (minimum 5 pairs). Descriptive ranking: Bootstrap resample events (500 draws, seed 42); rank by observed report-row count and observed reported volume with intervals on those metrics (not rank positions, not rainfall-normalized). Quality flags: Missingness, implausible values, quarantine status; aggregate flag counts in results/qa_flags.json with a unit and definition for every flag. Missingness counts are identifiers with >50% missing within-identifier measurements (78 for each measurement); other flags count report rows. Separate HTML tables prevent mixing units. The full feed contains 16,720 report rows, with 8,058 missing volume or rainfall and 176 unique quarantined rows. Report-row flags overlap; their sum is not a unique exclusion count. Individual identifiers and measurements are withheld. Evaluation: Train 2022 to 2023, validation 2024 (pooled with train for fitting), test 2025. Pooled RMSE on identical model-scorable paired report rows; Spearman over outfall union with event-level bootstrap resampling train+validation events while holding 2025 counts fixed. 5. Results ¶ See RESULTS.md (regenerated by cso-insight run --root . ). The mean-volume baseline achieves lower pooled RMSE than the log1p rainfall model on held-out paired events. Spearman correlation compares raw event counts, not rainfall-normalized ranks. Rain threshold is an event-conditional positive rate among events with known rainfall; positive means at or above the 2022-2024 training 75th percentile, with at least three eligible training rainfall observations. Of 1,643 eligible known-rainfall test rows, 1,635 are supported; eight rows across five identifiers default negative and stay in the denominator. Missing test rainfall is excluded. Five rows equal the threshold; the fraction is 395/1,643. It does not measure overflow detection or accuracy on non-event days. Scoring covers 1,625 of 1,643 eligible paired test reports and 1,625 of 3,075 eligible test reports. Eighteen paired reports across ten IDs have no supported training model. Support exclusions are exported; the baseline is evaluated on the same subset. Minimum five pairs and variable training rainfall are required. 6. Limitations ¶ Not Metro Vancouver data; transfer requires local validation. Missing measurements on many rows; descriptive totals reflect reporting coverage. Volume cap excludes 156 evaluation-period reports (159 full feed), removing 32.1% of 2022-2025 reported volume after other eligibility rules relative to the same cohort without the volume cap. It can change top-five volume priorities; see capped/uncapped ranks in the cohort ledger. Log1p-linear model ignores antecedent moisture and system hydraulics; inverse transform can extrapolate beyond observed volumes. Bootstrap intervals treat events as independent; storm-date clustering is not modelled. Intervals omit fitting uncertainty and measurement error. Notification timestamps may lag actual overflow start. 2026 partial year excluded but present in raw feed. Preregistration was amended after results were seen. 7. Reproducibility ¶ pip install -r requirements-lock.txt pip install --no-deps -e . ./scripts/download_data.sh cso-insight run --root . Preregistration SHA-256: see docs/PREREGISTRATION.sha256 . Amendment after review: docs/PREREGISTRATION_AMENDMENT_2026-10-01.md . References ¶ McGrath, G., et al. (2019). Network Topology and Rainfall Controls on the Variability of Combined Sewer Overflows and Loads. Water Resources Research . https://doi.org/10.1029/2019WR025336 EPA SWMM. https://www.epa.gov/water-research/storm-water-management-model-swmm McDonnell et al. (2020). PySWMM. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.02292 Massachusetts EEA CSO feed. https://openamend.org/data/EEADP_CSO.csv AMEND dashboard. https://openamend.org/dashboard.html Metro Vancouver sewer overflow map. https://metrovancouver.org/services/liquid-waste/real-time-sewer-overflow-map Regional validation checklist ¶ Before applying these methods to a regional agency: obtain a permitted local feed; define reporting-stage reconciliation with the data owner; verify units, timestamps, unknown identifiers and completeness; predeclare filters and storm-level validation; compare against a simple baseline on the same supported cohort; and validate the actual decision with utility engineers. This work supplies no firm client reference, Metro Vancouver validation, or operational forecast. The frozen plan hash verifies content integrity and does not establish chronology. See frozen analysis plan, amended retrospectively for the default wrapper and recorded amendments.
